message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **TL;DR** – Use the `gcloud` CLI (recommended) or the REST API (if you need to embed it in a script or CI pipeline).

---

## 1.  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Pick a project, zone, and machine type
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"   # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM

# 2️⃣  Pick a GPU type and count
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1

# 3️⃣  Pick a boot‑disk image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS)
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# 4️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project="${PROJECT}" \
  --zone="${ZONE}" \
  --machine-type="${MACHINE_TYPE}" \
  --accelerator="type=${GPU_TYPE},count=${GPU_COUNT}" \
  --image-family="${IMAGE_FAMILY}" \
  --image-project="${IMAGE_PROJECT}" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=allow-ssh,allow-http,allow-https \
  --service-account=my-service-account@${PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation |
| `--accelerator` | Attach the RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk |
| `--boot-disk-type=pd-ssd` | SSD for fast I/O |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script that installs NVIDIA drivers after boot |
| `--scopes` | Full Cloud Platform access (adjust if you need tighter scopes) |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules (e.g., allow SSH) |
| `--service-account` | IAM service account to run the instance |

#### Optional: Install NVIDIA drivers automatically

Create a file called `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
# Reboot to load the driver
sudo reboot
```

Make it executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

The `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` flag will run this script on first boot.

---

## 2.  REST API (curl example)

If you prefer to use the raw Compute Engine REST API, here’s a minimal example.  
You’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope.

```bash
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 1️⃣  Build the JSON payload
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\\napt-get update\\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "my-service-account@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["allow-ssh", "allow-http", "allow-https"]
  }
}
EOF

# 2️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### Notes

- **Quotas** – RTX A6000 GPUs are a premium resource. Make sure your project has the necessary GPU quota in the chosen zone (`us-central1-a` in the example).
- **Billing** – GPU usage is billed hourly. Verify that billing is enabled for your project.
- **Firewall** – The tags `allow-ssh`, `allow-http`, `allow-https` assume you have corresponding firewall rules. If not, create them:

  ```bash
  gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-ssh \
    --allow tcp:22 \
    --target-tags allow-ssh \
    --description "Allow SSH"

  gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-http \
    --allow tcp:80 \
    --target-tags allow-http \
    --description "Allow HTTP"

  gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-https \
    --allow tcp:443 \
    --target-tags allow-https \
    --description "Allow HTTPS"
  ```

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| 1 | Enable **Compute Engine API** in the Cloud Console. |
| 2 | Ensure you have **GPU quota** for `nvidia-a6000` in the target zone. |
| 3 | Create or select a **service account** with the required scopes. |
| 4 | (Optional) Create **firewall rules** for SSH/HTTP/HTTPS. |
| 5 | Run the `gcloud` command or the REST API call. |
| 6 | Verify the instance appears in the **Compute Engine** dashboard. |
| 7 | SSH into the instance and confirm the GPU is visible: `nvidia-smi`. |

That’s it! Once the instance is running, you’ll have a powerful Ubuntu 20.04 machine with an RTX A6000 GPU ready for deep‑learning, rendering, or any GPU‑heavy workload.
